## The core idea

Kelly defines a **true fan** as a fan who will buy anything you produce. His examples are vivid: they drive 200 miles to see you sing, buy the hardback, paperback and audio versions of your book, purchase your next figurine sight unseen, or pay for a "best-of" DVD of a channel you give away free. The 2008 original adds details such as setting a Google Alert for your name and buying the box set even when they own the low-resolution version.

The claim is that roughly a thousand such people let you make **a living, not a fortune**. Why is that exciting? Because a thousand is a human-scale target. You might remember a thousand names, and adding one new true fan a day would take only a few years. Millions of paying fans, by contrast, is not a realistic goal when starting out.

The essay frames this as an alternative to chasing stardom: the narrow peaks of platinum hits and blockbusters.
